title: Confirm the pilot sector and local community needs
body:
## Outcome

Choose a small first area that people can maintain, and test whether joinable climbing sessions solve the local problem.

## Scope

- [ ] Interview five to eight local climbers, including people who are new to Chattanooga.
- [ ] Choose one Stone Fort sector and identify two potential field reviewers.
- [ ] Identify the exact climbing area meant by St. Elmo before publishing it.
- [ ] Record the first supported grade ranges, session scenarios, and proposed success measures.
- [ ] Confirm the Crag Conditions URL with its owner; the supplied candidate page describes UK coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A written scope names the pilot sector and community workflows.
- [ ] Interview findings distinguish real needs from assumptions.
- [ ] A person accepts responsibility for catalog corrections and community moderation.

## Dependencies

Can start independently.

Priority: P0. Milestone: M0 Data feasibility.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Audit data rights and assemble a reviewed pilot catalog
body:
## Outcome

Establish a legal and maintainable source of useful climb facts before building route recommendations.

## Scope

- [ ] Audit a sample of current OpenBeta coverage and retain field-level provenance.
- [ ] Complete the source register, including storage, display, model processing, map derivatives, and export rights.
- [ ] Document permission requirements for any supplied PDFs; keep restricted originals private.
- [ ] Collect original observations where permitted sources are incomplete.
- [ ] Review 30 to 60 candidate climbs with stable IDs, discipline-specific grades, aliases, and uncertainty.
- [ ] Define import dry runs, duplicate resolution, revisions, withdrawal, and cache invalidation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every published field has approved provenance and permitted intended uses.
- [ ] No Mountain Project scrape, unlicensed PDF content, or restricted photos enter the repository.
- [ ] The pack contains relevant warmups and projects for the pilot group.
- [ ] Unknown coordinates and disputed grades remain explicit rather than guessed.

## Dependencies

Backlog E01

Priority: P0. Milestone: M0 Data feasibility.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Scaffold the application and prove Docker deployment and restoration
body:
## Outcome

Create the smallest reproducible application on the existing VPS, with a recovery procedure that has been exercised.

## Scope

- [ ] Confirm stack choice, VPS resources, operating system, domain, reverse proxy, and backup destination.
- [ ] Add Django and PostgreSQL with locked dependencies, Dockerfile, compose.yaml, and placeholder-only .env.example.
- [ ] Configure health checks, private database networking, TLS integration, secure sessions, and production settings.
- [ ] Add actual development, test, and migration commands to README and AGENTS.md.
- [ ] Add CI for the application and configure private vulnerability reporting.
- [ ] Document updates, controlled migrations, encrypted off-host backups, and rollback.
- [ ] Restore a backup into an isolated instance and measure recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean checkout starts with documented commands and no embedded secrets.
- [ ] Only intended proxy ports are publicly reachable.
- [ ] Database and approved media survive container replacement.
- [ ] An isolated restore recovers representative records and media.

## Dependencies

Can start independently.

Priority: P0. Milestone: M1 Community foundation.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Build pseudonymous profiles and joinable climbing outings
body:
## Outcome

Help a climber with few local connections find and join an outing with clear expectations.

## Scope

- [ ] Implement lightweight accounts, password recovery design, and pseudonymous profiles without identity or skill verification.
- [ ] Separate comfortable and project grades by discipline and permit optional availability and interests.
- [ ] Create area-filtered and date-filtered outing cards with capacity, join policy, meeting visibility, and time zone.
- [ ] Implement requested, accepted, declined, withdrawn, and waitlisted participation states.
- [ ] Support edits, cancellation, and in-app notifications for accepted participants.
- [ ] Default precise meetup details and participant lists to accepted participants.
- [ ] Test private-plan authorization and concurrent capacity updates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new member can find an outing, request to join, and see appropriate details after acceptance.
- [ ] Public viewers cannot access private details through pages, APIs, or exports.
- [ ] Concurrent joins cannot exceed capacity or create duplicates.
- [ ] Cancellation and material changes are visible to participants.

## Dependencies

Backlog E03

Priority: P0. Milestone: M1 Community foundation.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Add discussion moderation and member privacy controls
body:
## Outcome

Keep a small local forum usable without relying on real-name verification or automated skill ratings.

## Scope

- [ ] Add the four initial discussion categories and replies with safe rendering.
- [ ] Implement report, block, removal, suspension, and moderation audit records.
- [ ] Define contribution terms, privacy notice, proposed age policy, deletion behavior, and log retention.
- [ ] Add abuse limits for signup, login, posts, uploads, and expensive endpoints.
- [ ] Assign moderation coverage and escalation for sensitive access reports.
- [ ] Keep member content outside public dataset exports and model context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A moderator can handle a report and audit the action.
- [ ] Blocking and visibility are enforced server-side.
- [ ] Malicious HTML and oversized content are rejected or rendered safely.
- [ ] The deletion and backup-retention behavior matches the published notice.

## Dependencies

Backlog E03, Backlog E04

Priority: P0. Milestone: M1 Community foundation.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Build and field-check the deterministic planner and map exports
body:
## Outcome

Produce a useful warmup-to-project itinerary and PNG without any model call or paid map dependency.

## Scope

- [ ] Create area, feature, climb, source, access, and trail-graph models with review states.
- [ ] Implement contextual name and alias resolution and discipline-specific grade ordering.
- [ ] Filter closures and unsupported records before scoring candidate itineraries.
- [ ] Respect a fixed project, editable time budget, walking preferences, and a return path.
- [ ] Require reviewed trail edges for every navigable leg; fail usefully on disconnection.
- [ ] Render an original SVG-to-PNG map or explicitly non-scale schematic with sources, dates, stop labels, and current-plan link.
- [ ] Version saved plans and invalidate dependent caches when access or permission changes.
- [ ] Have two local reviewers independently check paths and stop identification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Form-based planning works with no model credentials.
- [ ] Every selected climb and trail edge belongs to the approved pack and meets hard constraints.
- [ ] Closed or revoked records never appear as eligible stops.
- [ ] Phone-readable exports match the saved plan and exclude unauthorized private details.
- [ ] Field review resolves ambiguous junctions before navigable coverage is advertised.

## Dependencies

Backlog E02, Backlog E03

Priority: P0. Milestone: M2 Reviewed session planner.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Add constrained conversational planning and hard spending limits
body:
## Outcome

Allow natural-language preferences while preserving deterministic planning and predictable operating costs.

## Scope

- [ ] Define typed parsing and explanation schemas and a replaceable provider adapter.
- [ ] Limit context to approved public catalog data and the necessary preferences.
- [ ] Validate all model-returned identifiers and treat retrieved text as untrusted.
- [ ] Add timeout, output, retry, per-user, and site-wide limits.
- [ ] Reserve request budget atomically before provider calls and settle measured usage afterward.
- [ ] Use revision-aware, privacy-scoped caching and fall back to structured planning.
- [ ] Evaluate realistic requests, ambiguous names, prompt injection, invalid IDs, outages, and concurrent budget use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No known closure violations or fabricated IDs are accepted in the evaluation suite.
- [ ] An exhausted budget or provider outage leaves core planning available.
- [ ] Concurrent requests cannot exceed the configured reservation cap.
- [ ] Private member messages and full profiles never enter model prompts.

## Dependencies

Backlog E06

Priority: P1. Milestone: M3 Conversational pilot.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).

title: Run the local pilot and decide whether to expand
body:
## Outcome

Validate that people actually meet and climb together before adding many more crags.

## Scope

- [ ] Invite roughly 10 to 20 climbers and arrange several voluntarily hosted sessions.
- [ ] Measure useful plans, accepted joins, self-reported completed outings, repeat use, and correction workload.
- [ ] Check actual VPS latency, export readability, model spend, backups, and moderation response.
- [ ] Review a four-week pilot against the documented goals and interview participants.
- [ ] Resolve wrong-location, access, and privacy issues before public expansion.
- [ ] Choose the next sector or area based on demand, permissions, field data, and maintenance ownership.
- [ ] Create a separate rope-climbing requirements issue before implementing Leda or Foster Falls planning.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pilot findings and an explicit continue, revise, or pause decision are documented.
- [ ] There are no unresolved material location, access, or privacy defects.
- [ ] Every proposed new area has a source plan and maintenance owner.
- [ ] Expansion is based on evidence rather than geographic coverage alone.

## Dependencies

Backlog E04, Backlog E05, Backlog E06, Backlog E07

Priority: P1. Milestone: M3 Conversational pilot.

Reference: [project plan](https://github.com/Dyno-man/Crag-Commune/blob/main/docs/planning/PROJECT_PLAN.md).
